subject: BrightGrid implementation handoff — cost & performance priorities
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Evan Torres <evan.torres@brightgrid.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: BrightGrid implementation handoff — cost/perf focus

Hi team — looping you all in for the formal handoff. BrightGrid is moving into the implementation window and asked us to prioritize cost controls and predictable latency for their search/summarization flow. Key context: production qps expected ~120–250, peak bursts to 400 for campaign windows, latency SLO 200–300ms p95, and they prefer single-model routing with quantized variants for cost gating.

Attachments: BrightGrid_Kickoff_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf), BrightGrid_perf_requirements.csv (csv)

Ask: Mina/Marissa — can you lead the implementation cadence? High-level items to cover in the first week:
- Confirm sample payloads (batch size / tokens) and traffic shape
- Recommend quantization profile and fallback plan
- Define KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts
- Routing policy for low-cost vs low-latency variants

I'll hand off the existing SOW and hubspot deal (BG-9241). Sara, if you can confirm the final latency target and any compliance constraints (e.g., data residency), that will help the plan.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Evan Torres <evan.torres@brightgrid.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightGrid implementation handoff — cost & performance priorities

Thanks Aditya — taking lead on the implementation side. Quick plan below; will set the first sync for Tuesday and propose an internal pre-kick to align engineers.

Proposed first-week checklist (owner in parentheses):
1) Telemetry & payloads (BrightGrid / Mina) — we need 48 hours of representative logs or a sample of 5000 requests with token counts. Please share sample payloads as NDJSON.
2) Latency SLA confirmation (BrightGrid) — you noted 200–300ms p95; confirm if p50/p95 both must be under 300ms or only p95. (Sara)
3) Quantization profile recommendation (Mina) — will propose two profiles: int8-safe for baseline cost and int4-aggressive for nightly job runs; list expected token-cost delta.
4) Batching & KV policy (Marissa/Mina) — default batch target and max latency; prefix caching rules for repeated prefixes (search idempotent flows).
5) Routing policy (Mina) — policy doc that routes: low-latency variant in region A for 95% of requests, fallback to low-cost quantized variant when utilization>85%.

I've attached an initial sample payload file to speed validation: BrightGrid_sample_payloads.ndjson (ndjson). I'll also link a short multistep evaluation we'll run to ensure quality doesn't regress with int4.

Proposed sync times (please pick one):
- Tue 2026-08-17 09:00 PT
- Tue 2026-08-17 11:00 PT
- Wed 2026-08-18 08:00 PT (backup)

Sara — if you can confirm the sample payload drop and the SLO clarification today, we'll run a prep pass and share quantization cost estimates ahead of the sync.

Attachments: BrightGrid_sample_payloads.ndjson (ndjson)

Best,
Mina Haddad
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Evan Torres <evan.torres@brightgrid.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightGrid implementation handoff — cost & performance priorities

Thanks Mina — quick operational notes from CS perspective:
- I'll own the onboarding timeline and run the mutual action plan (MAP). I'll add Milestones: Kickoff, Stage 1 (sample validation), Stage 2 (quantization trials), Stage 3 (canary + rollout).
- For batching defaults, propose starting with an adaptive batch target of 16 requests / max latency 60ms on the serving side to meet p95. We'll adjust after we see token distribution.
- For KV caching: recommend a 30s TTL for top-10 repeated prefixes, with a cache bypass option for freshness-sensitive flows.

Action items assigned:
- BrightGrid: share 5k sample requests + expected peak hourly qps (Sara)
- Mina: produce a one-pager quant profile comparison (int8 vs int4) by Monday EOD
- Marissa: create MAP doc and share HubSpot link to track progress

I'll draft the MAP and post the link to the Drive before the sync.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Li <sara.li@brightgrid.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Torres <evan.torres@brightgrid.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightGrid implementation handoff — cost & performance priorities

Hi all — thanks for the clear plan. Confirming: BrightGrid can provide the 5k sample payloads and the hourly qps histogram by EOD Monday (2026-08-16). Latency SLO: p95 <= 275ms is our goal; p50 can be anything under 160ms but not a hard requirement.

A couple of asks from BrightGrid security: we need to confirm where KV cache hashes are stored (no PII), and whether quantized models will run in-region (US-West) only — we have data residency rules for a subset of users. Also attaching the internal onboarding doc for context.

Attachments: BrightGrid_internal_onboard_notes.pdf (pdf)

Available for the proposed Tue 09:00 PT sync.

Sara Li
Head of ML Platform, BrightGrid
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Evan Torres <evan.torres@brightgrid.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: BrightGrid MAP + next steps (quant profiles & routing policy)

Following our sync, attaching the mutual action plan and summarizing decisions so we have a single source of truth:
- Confirmed SLO: p95 <= 275ms (BrightGrid)
- Sample payloads received and validated (5,000 reqs). Token distribution attached to Drive.
- Quant profiles:
  • Profile A (int8-safe) — expected cost delta ~ -28% vs fp16, quality delta negligible on eval set.
  • Profile B (int4-aggressive) — expected cost delta ~ -52%; will run nightly jobs only and used as fallback for non-interactive batch flows.
- Batching: start with adaptive batch target = 16, max batch latency = 60ms. We'll revisit after canary.
- KV caching: 30s TTL for top prefixes; hashes stored in customer-managed Redis in US-West (no PII).
- Routing policy: primary: low-latency model (Profile A) in US-West. Fallback: Profile B in same region when utilization>85% or error-rate rises >1.5%. Cross-region fallbacks only on regional outage.

Attachments uploaded to Drive and HubSpot MAP updated: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1BrightGridOnboard
DocSign SOW sent for signature (link in HubSpot).

Next steps (owners):
- Mina: run int8 vs int4 eval on the 1k validation set and post results (ETA 48 hours)
- Marissa: schedule canary for Tue next week and coordinate logs/alerting
- BrightGrid (Sara): confirm Redis details and provide onboarding VPN creds for staging

Thanks everyone — this gives us a clear runway for a canary next week.

Mina Haddad
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
